channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: A empresários, Lula diz que estabilidade fiscal é obrigatória e defende reforma do Judiciário
item.description: During a speech to businesspeople in São Paulo, Lula defended fiscal stability as mandatory, proposed Judiciary reform, and criticized regulatory agencies, while attacking Banco Master's owner Daniel Vorcaro. The president reiterated economic positions amid debate with the business community.

item.title: Veja propostas dos candidatos ao governo de São Paulo para o Meio Ambiente
item.description: With the 2026 São Paulo elections approaching, candidates present proposals focused on the environmental crisis, including river recovery such as the Tietê, universal access to basic sanitation, and punishment of polluting companies. The agendas are influenced by recent climate events, such as heavy rains causing floods and deaths in several cities across the state. Each candidate outlines their environmental priorities, emphasizing the integration of sectoral policies into state development.

item.title: Inelegível, Arruda gastou R$ 1,3 milhão com militância durante campanha
item.description: José Roberto Arruda (PSD), disqualified by the TSE due to administrative improbity convictions, spent R$2.3 million over 40 days of campaigning, with R$1.3 million (56.8%) allocated to street activism. Although his candidacy was annulled, his name remains on the ballot, but votes will be voided.

item.title: Influencers podem divulgar intenção de votos nas redes? Veja regras do TSE
item.description: TSE regulations allow influencers to spontaneously share their voting intentions before election day, but prohibit new electoral advertising posts on election day. The rules also ban paid engagements for political content or self-funded promotion. Examples include influencers with hundreds of thousands of followers sharing their candidate lists.

item.title: Marina Sena faz aniversário, mas fãs brasilienses que ganham o presente
item.description: Marina Sena celebrates her 30th birthday, musically inspired by Gal Costa, and is confirmed as a headliner at the 2026 Festival Estilo Brasil. A native of Taiobeiras in northern Minas Gerais, she stands out with her high-pitched voice and sensuality, with hits like 'Por Supuesto' and 'Dano Sarrada' solidifying her status in the new generation of Brazilian pop.

item.title: Governo Lula gastará até R$ 15 bi para perdoar 90% em dívidas
item.description: The Lula administration launched Desenrola 3.0, a program that will forgive 90% of citizens' debts, with an estimated cost of up to R$15 billion. Targeted at families with debts overdue between 2 and 4.5 years, the initiative may impact public accounts and is subject to fiscal rules. The measure is announced 9 days before the first round of elections.

item.title: Lula brinca e chama Joesley, da JBS, de “empresário desaforado”
item.description: President Lula joked with Joesley Batista, JBS owner, calling him an 'unbalanced businessman' at a dinner with entrepreneurs in São Paulo. The PT leader criticized his involvement in the defense sector and emphasized the need for partnerships to grow the country. The meeting was the second with business leaders in under 30 days and was organized by a group linked to government allies.

item.title: Lula critica home office nas agências reguladoras
item.description: President Lula criticized the remote work model in regulatory agencies, arguing it hampers oversight. He stressed the need to reinforce the State's role in guiding public policies. The meeting is part of a series of dialogues with business leaders on economic and governance issues.

item.title: Alta nos gastos públicos exigirá sacrifícios
item.description: Brazilian public spending is projected to reach 19.55% of GDP in 2024, the highest level since the 2020 pandemic, according to the finance ministry's forecasts. The sharp deterioration in public accounts demands fiscal adjustments, even if they require popular sacrifices. In 2023, President Lula's government already incurred high costs to settle court-ordered debt payments.

item.title: Porque a aposta eleitoral de Lula no fim das bets pode dar em nada
item.description: President Lula expressed surprise at the negative impact of 'bets' on Brazilian families' budgets, despite four years in office. The criticism seems more of an electoral strategy than genuine concern, especially with upcoming elections. The defense of sports betting may not attract the expected electorate.

item.title: A próxima pesquisa Quaest antes do debate presidencial da TV Globo
item.description: Quaest will release a new poll on Monday before the TV Globo presidential debate on Thursday. The survey of 2,004 voters measures the impact of Lula's gambling ban announcement. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro remain tied in the first round (37% and 33%) and in a technical tie in the second round.

item.title: Trump aposta que vai ser “dono da América Latina”, diz Lula
item.description: Lula criticized Trump for attempting to dominate Latin America and questioned his handling of the Iran war.

item.title: Datafolha, 2º turno: veja os grupos em que a disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro está mais apertada
item.description: Datafolha polls Lula at 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 45% in a 2nd-round tie. The race is tight across most demographic groups, except in the Northeast where Lula leads by 31 points.

item.title: Bets e 'jogo do tigrinho' proibidos: tudo o que você precisa saber em 11 pontos
item.description: The federal government, through a provisional decree signed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, banned online betting and virtual games such as 'jogo do tigrinho', with a deadline for withdrawing balances by October 5 and site blocking starting October 6.

item.title: MAPA: Quaest mostra como está a disputa presidencial nos estados
item.description: Quaest polls show the 2026 presidential race: Lula leads in 9 states, Flávio Bolsonaro leads in 8, and there are technical ties in 8 locations. The margin of error is 3 points, except São Paulo (2 points).

item.title: VÍDEO: Por que existem duas casas no Congresso?
item.description: The National Congress is composed of two chambers: the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate. The Chamber represents the Brazilian population, while the Senate ensures equal representation for all states. Both participate in lawmaking but have distinct roles, such as the impeachment process and review of presidential appointments.

item.title: Eleições 2026: em quantos candidatos o eleitor terá que votar?
item.description: In the 2026 Brazilian election, voters will cast ballots for six positions in the first round: federal deputy, state or district deputy, two senators, governor, and president. The voting order at the ballot box is predetermined and follows a specific sequence, with attention to confirming each candidate's details. Voters must select different names for the two Senate seats, otherwise the second vote will be invalidated.

item.title: Eleição no Sudeste: Veja os números da Quaest para os governos de São Paulo, Rio, Minas e Espírito Santo
item.description: Quaest surveys show clear leads for Southeast governors in 2026: Tarcísio (SP) at 44%, Paes (RJ) at 36%, Azevedo (MG) at 37%, and Ferraço (ES) at 33%. The polls reflect changes from previous surveys, with a 2-point margin of error in São Paulo and 3 points in other states.

item.title: MP do fim das bets precisa ser votada em até 120 dias; veja próximos passos
item.description: President Lula signed a provisional measure banning bets in Brazil, initially valid for four months and requiring congressional approval for permanent effect. The measure takes effect immediately with website blocks scheduled for October 6, allowing only balance withdrawals by then. Legislative progress depends on scheduling and leadership decisions after the first electoral round.

item.title: Lula defende IA brasileira para sair de disputa entre EUA e China
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva advocated for the development of Brazilian artificial intelligence and the construction of national data centers to avoid dependence on the technological rivalry between the United States and China. He emphasized the importance of exploiting critical minerals autonomously, with control and technology transfer, and reiterated support for investments in education.

item.title: Vamos fazer outra reforma do Judiciário, diz Lula em jantar com empresários em São Paulo
item.description: Lula stated at a dinner with business leaders in São Paulo that he will push for a judiciary reform and a 'true political reform,' recalling his role in creating the CNJ. He also advocated for domestic mining of critical minerals and criticized Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, calling him a 'scoundrel'.

item.title: Como vai funcionar a proibição das bets e qual seu impacto na eleição
item.description: President Lula signed a provisional decree banning online betting platforms in Brazil, with users allowed to cash out balances until October 5th and platforms required to shut down by October 6th. The measure was issued nine days before the first round of the 2026 elections, amid the electoral race against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Buscas no Google por Nossa Senhora e Flávio aumentam após fake news
item.description: Google searches for 'Nossa Senhora Aparecida' and 'Flávio Bolsonaro' surged after false news linked the presidential candidate to plans to remove the title of patron saint of Brazil from the image of the Virgin. Minister André Mendonça ordered the removal of false posts on digital platforms. Flávio denied the accusations in a video posted on X, reaffirming respect for all religions.

item.title: ‘Quem paga o preço do desajuste fiscal é o povo pobre’, diz Lula em meio à promessa de melhora das contas
item.description: President Lula stated that fiscal responsibility is a government obligation and that budget imbalances primarily affect the poor. He criticized demands on the current administration, recalling he took office with a 2.8% deficit, and emphasized the importance of not spending more than revenue.

item.title: Lula promete reforma do Judiciário e ataca Vorcaro em jantar com empresários
item.description: Lula proposed Judiciary reform and attacked Daniel Vorcaro during a dinner with business leaders in São Paulo, nine days before the first round. At the event, the president criticized Vorcaro over alleged improper relations with Supreme Court justices and called for thorough investigations without distinction. The gathering included over 686 businesspeople and government officials.

item.title: Lula diz que nunca viu “podridão” como a que acontece no Supremo
item.description: Lula harshly criticized the Supreme Federal Court during a meeting with business leaders in São Paulo, using terms like 'rotten' and accusing Minister Alexandre de Moraes of corrupting people with money and 'lust'. He argued that society should decide on judges' terms and also attacked potential future governments, defending the preservation of Brazil's natural resources.

item.title: Lula fala em reforma do Judiciário e admite discutir mandato para ministros do STF
item.description: At a dinner hosted by the Esfera e Prerrogativas group, President Lula criticized the Master case and proposed discussing the establishment of terms for Supreme Court justices, advocating punishment for those who made mistakes. He highlighted the Judiciary reform carried out during his administration and suggested re-election of ministers instead of lifetime terms.

item.title: Em jantar com empresários, Lula diz que é preciso 'escolher entre democracia ou barbárie' e fala em conciliar 'responsabilidade fiscal com social'
item.description: At a dinner with business leaders, Lula warned about choosing between democracy and barbarism, advocating for balancing fiscal responsibility with social policies. He highlighted his history of responsible fiscal management and avoided committing to lowering interest rates or spending, attributing such demands to the market and the Central Bank's independence. Lula also criticized Donald Trump and promised political and Judiciary reforms in a potential fourth term.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro vê estrago com notícia falsa sobre Nossa Senhora e tenta conter danos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign had to refute a false news story claiming he would remove Our Lady of Aparecida's title as Brazil's patron saint, damaging his campaign's image. The lie spread rapidly on social media and required a quick response to mitigate political harm.

item.title: Dino deve devolver relatório sobre Moraes a julgamento após 2º turno, dizem aliados
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino is expected to return the report on Daniel Vorcaro's messages to Alexandre de Moraes for trial only after the second round of the 2026 elections. According to allies, he believes that resuming the discussion before the elections could cause a crisis in the court and influence the vote.

item.title: Lula encontra empresários em evento em São Paulo após proibir bets
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva met with over 500 business leaders in São Paulo, following the ban on betting, at an event that gathered leaders from various economic sectors. The meeting emphasized dialogue between government and business, focusing on economic issues and development. The presence of prominent figures reinforced the importance of discussing public policies and growth.

item.title: Governo precisará compensar perda de R$ 6,8 bi em receitas com bets até 2027, diz ministro
item.description: The federal government will need to offset a loss of R$ 6.8 billion in revenue from online betting until 2027, following the ban on the activity. According to Minister Bruno Moretti, the 2027 budget draft will see adjustments to redirect R$ 5 billion to the Desenrola 3.0 program and seek new revenue sources.

item.title: Governo vai usar IA e canal de denúncia para derrubar sites de apostas
item.description: The Lula government announced the use of artificial intelligence and a complaint channel to identify and combat illegal betting sites in Brazil. The measure is part of an offensive against unregulated betting in the country.

item.title: Entenda como vai funciona o novo Desenrola, que prevê desconto de até 90% nas dívidas
item.description: The Lula government launched the third phase of Desenrola Brasil, a program offering up to 90% discounts for indebted individuals, with changes from previous versions. The announcement took place in São Paulo, just before the 2026 presidential elections.

item.title: Mendonça derruba posts de Erika Hilton e Leonardo Boff sobre Nossa Senhora
item.description: TSE vice-president Minister André Mendonça removed a post by actor Antonio Tabet at the request of Flávio Bolsonaro, escalating a series of posts related to Our Lady. The action was criticized for allegedly censoring religious statements in the electoral context.

item.title: Leia a íntegra da medida provisória que acaba com as bets no Brasil
item.description: President Lula published a provisional measure banning online betting houses, known as 'bets', with immediate effect. The measure aims to combat family debt and gambling addiction, but must be approved by Congress within 120 days. Lula justified the decision by comparing gambling addiction to crack and emphasized the need for a drastic solution.

item.title: Funcionário do Planalto estimula fake news sobre Nossa Senhora
item.description: George Marques, the coordinator of Strategy and Information at the Presidency's Secretariat of Communication, shared a false news story claiming that the PL and Flávio Bolsonaro were behind a project to strip Nossa Senhora Aparecida of her title as patron saint of Brazil. The post was removed after a court order from Minister André Mendonça of the TSE. Marques denied agreeing with the content, saying the sharing was unintentional.

item.title: Confira como foi a sexta-feira (25) dos presidenciáveis
item.description: On Friday (25), presidential candidates carried out campaigns across the country with walks, parades, and events with supporters. Lula advocated for banning sports betting sites, while Caiado emphasized debt renegotiation and subsidies for agribusiness. Candidates also addressed topics such as education, security, and the environment during their rallies and interviews.

item.title: STF condena Eduardo Bolsonaro por difamação contra Tabata Amaral
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court convicted former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro for defamation against lawmaker Tabata Amaral, imposing a one-year prison sentence and $80,000 in fines. The case involved social media posts about Tabata's bill regarding feminine hygiene products. Justice Alexandre de Moraes served as the rapporteur.

item.title: Fake news da padroeira pode virar tiro no pé para Lula com católicos
item.description: A fake news about Nossa Senhora Aparecida sparked controversy between Catholics and evangelicals on social media, potentially hurting Lula by losing Catholic Church support. Analysts discuss the strategy's impact, Alckmin's stance, and the 2026 religious vote competition.

item.title: O encontro de Lula e Joesley Batista
item.description: President Lula attended a dinner with business leaders in São Paulo, including Joesley Batista and Rubens Ometto, following the announcement of a ban on bets in the country. The event gathered figures from the productive sector and government allies such as Geraldo Alckmin and Fernando Haddad.

item.title: Lula compara vício em bets a crack e câncer para justificar proibição
item.description: President Lula compared online betting addiction to crack and cancer to justify banning bets through a provisional decree. The measure also criminalizes those who operate or advertise betting platforms.

item.title: Governo Lula fará força-tarefa para combater mercado ilegal de bets
item.description: The Lula government established a task force to combat the illegal online betting market, including a total ban on sports betting, website and bank account blocking, and asset seizure for public security. The provisional measure takes effect immediately and requires congressional approval within 120 days, enjoying strong public support among women and evangelicals ahead of the October 2026 election.

item.title: Tabet ironiza repercussão de post sobre Flávio: "Perdão, família miliciana"
item.description: Antonio Tabet posted an ironic criticism of Flávio Bolsonaro's family, accusing them of attacking Our Lady of Aparecida, which sparked widespread backlash. Following the reaction, TSE Minister André Mendonça ordered the removal of the post, deeming the accusation unfounded. Tabet later mocked the situation by asking for 'forgiveness' from the 'military family' amid the controversy.

item.title: Datafolha: como está a disputa entre Lula e Flávio em SP, MG, RJ, DF e PE
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows a technical tie between Lula and Flávio in Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, and the Federal District, while Flávio leads in São Paulo and Lula holds an advantage in Pernambuco. Nationally, both candidates remain tied with 40% and 36% of first-round voting intentions. The surveys were conducted between September 22 and 24, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points.

item.title: Quem pode tirar o título de padroeira do Brasil? Não é o presidente
item.description: The rumor that Flávio Bolsonaro proposed removing Our Lady of Aparecida as Brazil's patron saint went viral after the first round of elections. This false claim has circulated since 2018 without any factual basis. The Brazilian presidency has no authority to change the country's patron saint, as such a designation depends on a papal decree, not domestic political power.

item.title: Associação das bets diz que proibição pegou setor de surpresa
item.description: The National Association of Games and Lotteries (ANJL) criticized the provisional decree signed by Lula banning 'betting shops' in Brazil, calling it a political rather than technical decision, and announced plans for legal action, citing losses to investments and state revenue.

item.title: Apostas: governo publica MP que proíbe as bets no Brasil
item.description: The federal government published a provisional decree fully banning online betting houses in Brazil, including sports and virtual game bets. Additionally, the Desenrola 3.0 program was created to reduce family debts by purchasing financial institutions' debts with a minimum 90% discount and passing the benefit to debtors. The measure also extinguishes state and district concessions for fixed-bet lotteries.

item.title: Haddad diz que Lula “formou juízo” sobre bets
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) supported President Lula's announcement to ban online betting ('bets') in Brazil, stating the timing is appropriate. Haddad described the situation as a 'pandemic' affecting both the economy and public health. The announcement occurred during a business event in São Paulo.

item.title: Flávio tenta responsabilizar Lula por expansão das bets, enquanto outros rivais evitam comentar veto do governo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro criticized the MP banning sports betting and online gambling, attempting to link regulation to the Lula government using the 'father of Tigrinho' slogan. Other candidates like Augusto Cury and Ronaldo Caiado avoided direct stances, with Cury advocating for ending bets and Caiado criticizing partial solutions.
